about: The plants Westernesse knows, one record each (the owner, 5 November, late: one authoritative definition; organisms.json retired): what each looks like, where it grows (data/catalog/habitats.json), what is gathered from it (an item of the catalog), how much a stand gives, what it is good for; a stand of it is set where a country has its habitat: the plants written without an abundance, most particular first, two to a place at most; and beside them any with an abundance (one to ten), by that chance at each place.

willow.name: Willow
willow.stand: Willows lean out over the water here, grey-green, their roots in the bank and their long shoots trailing in the current.

source.notes: Willow bark breaks a fever; the herb-wives of every country know it.

willow.looks: Grey-green leaves, long whippy shoots, and roots in the bank.

sphagnum.name: Sphagnum moss
sphagnum.stand: Sphagnum moss lies in the wet hollows, red and green, holding water like a sponge: it binds a wound better than linen.

source.notes: Dried and packed into wounds, as field dressings have been.

sphagnum.looks: Red and green moss in the wet hollows, holding water like a sponge.

meadowsweet.name: Meadowsweet
meadowsweet.stand: Meadowsweet grows thick along the wet ground, a froth of cream flowers that smells of almonds and honey.

source.notes: For pain and the stomach; strewn on floors.

meadowsweet.looks: Froth of cream flowers, smelling of almonds.

yarrow.name: Yarrow
yarrow.stand: Yarrow grows in the grass at the wayside, flat white heads over feathery leaves: a soldier's herb, for cuts.
yarrow.looks: Flat pale flower heads above feathery leaves.

alder.name: Alder
alder.looks: Dark cone-like catkins and roots at the water line.

heather_plant.name: Heather
heather_plant.looks: Low wiry shrubs covered in tiny purple-pink bells.
heather_plant.stand: Heather covers the ground here, low and wiry, purple with its small bells: steeped, it eases an ache.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

dandelion_plant.name: Dandelion
dandelion_plant.looks: A rosette of toothed leaves and a bright yellow flower that goes to a clock of seed.
dandelion_plant.stand: Dandelions stand in the grass, yellow and seeding: a tea of them cleans the blood.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

comfrey_plant.name: Comfrey
comfrey_plant.looks: Tall hairy leaves and hanging bells of purple or cream, by wet ground.
comfrey_plant.stand: Comfrey grows rank by the water, hairy-leaved, its bells hanging: knitbone, the herb-wives call it.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

cloudberry_plant.name: Cloudberry
cloudberry_plant.looks: A low plant of the high bogs with a single amber berry like a raspberry.
cloudberry_plant.stand: Cloudberries grow low among the moss up here, one amber berry to a plant.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

goodberry_plant.name: Goodberry
goodberry_plant.looks: A bramble with small, glossy red berries that ripen sweet.
goodberry_plant.stand: A bramble of goodberries grows along the edge of the trees, the berries small and red.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

foxglove_plant.name: Foxglove
foxglove_plant.looks: A tall spire of hanging purple bells, speckled inside, over a rosette of soft leaves.
foxglove_plant.stand: Foxgloves stand tall at the wood's edge, purple bells speckled inside: they heal, prepared rightly, and kill otherwise.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

feverwort_plant.name: Feverwort
feverwort_plant.looks: A small plant with pale, bitter leaves and white flowers in a flat head.
feverwort_plant.stand: Feverwort grows here in the rough grass, bitter-leaved: the herb-wives dry it for a child's fever.

source.notes: The plant the herb-wives' feverwort is dried from.

kingsfoil_plant.name: Kingsfoil
kingsfoil_plant.looks: A low three-leaved herb with a clean, sharp scent when crushed.
kingsfoil_plant.stand: Kingsfoil grows in the shade here, three-leaved and sharp-scented when crushed: it is prized, and rare.

source.notes: Orsino's herb, a thing sold and used, here the plant it is gathered from.

selfheal_plant.name: Self-heal
selfheal_plant.stand: Self-heal grows low in the short turf here, its purple flower-heads like little clubs among the grass.
selfheal_plant.looks: A low creeping herb of short turf, with square stems and close heads of purple, lipped flowers.

source.notes: An author's own plant, added by its record alone (the owner, 6 November: the authoring experiment), with the item it gives (items.json, selfheal).
